questionText:
Match the database key concept in List I with its operational definition in List II:

List I:
(A) Primary Key
(B) Candidate Key
(C) Alternate Key
(D) Foreign Key

List II:
(I) The selected attribute that uniquely identifies each record and cannot accept NULL values
(II) Any attribute or minimal set of attributes possessing the potential to uniquely identify records
(III) A candidate key that was not selected to be the primary key
(IV) An attribute whose values are derived from and reference the primary key of another table

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Primary Key uniquely identifies (not null); Candidate is any unique identifier; Alternate is an unchosen candidate; Foreign references parent table.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
